headline: What to consider before buying land for a tiny home?
articleBody:
Thinking about buying land for your dream tiny home? That’s super exciting! But before you jump in, there are a few crucial things to think about to make sure your property assessment goes smoothly and you end up with the perfect spot. First up, zoning and local regulations are huge. Zen Tiny Homes has spent over a decade working with local agencies across San Diego County and Southern California, so we know that understanding these rules early on can save you a ton of headaches. You'll want to check if tiny homes, especially the type you're envisioning (mobile or on a foundation), are even permitted in that area. An ADU, for example, is a permanent structure tied to your property, while a mobile tiny house is personal property, and their rules differ. 

Then, there's the land itself. Topography, drainage, and even the existing power and water supply are key factors. Is the land too sloped? Where will your septic system go? Does it have easy access to utilities, or will you be looking at costly extensions? These practical details directly impact your build timeline and budget. We can help you identify potential challenges and opportunities during a site feasibility consultation. 

Access is another big one. Can a construction crew easily get to the site? Will your tiny home have a clear path for delivery if it’s built off-site? Don’t forget about the surrounding environment – privacy, views, and noise levels all contribute to your quality of life. It’s all about making sure the land supports the lifestyle you want, not just the structure itself. Getting a professional property assessment or site feasibility consultation early on can clarify all these points and help you make a truly informed decision.
